classification.difficultyReason: Nonroutine abstract reasoning about self-reference or a family of sets. Page 48 supplies subset membership; pages 49–50 supply intersection and complement. Page 50 distinguishes relative complement, supporting X∩Ā=X\A without assuming X is the ambient universal set.

inlines.text: be any non-empty set. Define the following set:

inlines.latex: \tau=\{A\subseteq X\text{ where }A=\varnothing\text{ or }X\cap\overline A\text{ is finite}\}.

answer.short: $X\subseteq X$ and $X\cap\overline X=\varnothing$, which is finite, so $X\in\tau$.
answer.worked:
Taking $A=X$, we have $X\subseteq X$ and
$$X\cap\overline X=\varnothing.$$
The empty set has zero elements and is finite, so $X$ satisfies the finite-complement condition. Hence $X\in\tau$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $X=\mathbb R$, describe geometrically the elements of $\tau$.

answer.short:
The empty set and the real line with finitely many points removed, including no points removed.

The missing points form the finite complement.
answer.worked:
The definition includes $\varnothing$ separately. Every other member $A$ satisfies
$$\mathbb R\cap\overline A=\mathbb R\setminus A,$$
which must be finite. Thus $A$ is the real line with finitely many points removed. Removing no points gives the whole real line, which is also included.
